title: School Holidays: Maker and Creator - 8 to 12 Years, Darling Square

longDescription:

That's exactly what Maker and Creator delivers at the Darling Square Library makerspace, right in the heart of Sydney.

Running throughout the April school holidays, these sessions are designed for kids aged 8–12 who love making things and want to get their hands on technology that usually lives behind glass. The makerspace is packed with the kind of equipment that makes jaws drop, and every session is different — so if you come back twice, you'll try something new both times.

Families can look forward to:
* Free two-hour hands-on sessions in a fully equipped library makerspace
* Robot battles using Edison bots and programmable Sphero and Ozobot challenges
* Wind tube experiments — watch your creations take flight
* LED circuits built with conductive tape — light things up from scratch
* Different activities each session so every visit is a fresh adventure

title: Featherdale Wildlife Park
description: Get nose-to-nose with wombats, hand-feed kangaroos and spot koalas up close at one of Sydney's best wildlife parks — a guaranteed hit with kids of every age.
longDescription:
Imagine watching your child kneel down and hold out a handful of food, and a kangaroo — a real, full-grown kangaroo — hops right up and eats from their palm. That moment is on offer every single day at Featherdale Wildlife Park in Doonside, and it never gets old no matter how many times you experience it.

Featherdale is home to over 1,700 animals across 260 species, with the emphasis firmly on hands-on encounters rather than distant viewing. Unlike larger, more commercial wildlife parks, Featherdale keeps things intimate and accessible — koalas are close enough to photograph properly, wombats waddle past at ground level, and the keepers are genuinely passionate about sharing what they know. It is consistently voted one of Sydney's best family days out, and the train connection from the city makes it surprisingly easy to reach.

Families can look forward to:
* Hand-feeding kangaroos and wallabies straight from your palm — an unforgettable experience for young children
* Getting genuinely close to koalas, wombats and Tasmanian devils in naturalistic, uncrowded settings
* Walk-through aviaries with native Australian birds swooping overhead
* Reptile encounters including snakes and lizards handled by experienced keepers
* Daily keeper talks and feeding presentations throughout the park
* Easy access by train — Blacktown station, then a short bus or taxi ride
* Open daily 9am–5pm — a full day out from a morning start
address: 217-229 Kildare Road, Doonside NSW 2767

title: Luna Park Sydney
description: Rides, fairy floss and harbour views — Luna Park is Sydney's most iconic family fun destination right on the water at Milsons Point.
longDescription:
There are very few places in Sydney where you can ride a roller coaster with the Sydney Harbour Bridge towering behind you and the Opera House gleaming in the distance. Luna Park on Milsons Point has been making that exact thing possible since 1935 — and nearly a century later, it remains one of the most joyful, photogenic family destinations in Australia.

Park entry is free — you only pay for rides — which makes it a surprisingly flexible outing. You can bring a picnic, sit on the grass with harbour views, and let the kids choose a handful of rides that suit their age and daring. For little ones there are dedicated junior rides; for braver kids and teens there are classic thrillers like the Rotor and the Wild Mouse roller coaster. The landmark Mr Moon face gate is one of the most photographed spots in Sydney, and the whole park carries an irresistible retro charm.

Families can look forward to:
* Free park entry — pay only for the rides you choose, with unlimited ride passes also available
* Classic thrill rides including roller coasters, the Rotor and the Hair Raiser for older kids
* Junior rides and gentle options for toddlers and pre-schoolers — including cars, boats and carousels
* Spectacular views of Sydney Harbour Bridge and Opera House from inside the park
* Fairy floss, popcorn and classic carnival games throughout the grounds
* Open school holidays, weekends and selected weekdays — check the website for current hours
* Arrive by ferry from Circular Quay for a truly memorable harbour approach
address: 1 Olympic Drive, Milsons Point NSW 2061

title: Centennial Parklands – Family Outdoor Fun

longDescription:
580 acres of parkland, smack in the middle of Sydney's Eastern Suburbs, free to visit every day of the year. Centennial Parklands is the kind of place that becomes a family ritual — the spot you go every Sunday morning, every school holiday, every time you need open air and green space and room to breathe.

The park has something for genuinely every age and energy level. Babies nap in prams along the wide paths while toddlers chase ducks at the ponds. Primary-age kids tear around the playgrounds and beg to hire bikes or pedal cars. Older children explore on foot, spot birds, or bring a ball for a kick in the vast open meadows. And parents get to sit on the grass and do absolutely nothing for an hour, which is also excellent.

Families can look forward to:
* Multiple free playgrounds suited to different age groups — from toddler-safe to big-kid climbing structures
* Feed the ducks, geese and swans at the iconic duck and goose ponds
* Hire bikes, tandems and pedal cars for a leisurely ride around the park (small hire fee)
* Wide open lawns perfect for picnics, cricket, kicking a ball or flying a kite
* Birdwatching — over 130 species recorded in the park, including ibis, herons and parrots
* Café on-site for breakfast and lunch — or BYO and use one of the free BBQ areas
* Open from sunrise to sunset every day — free always, for everyone

title: Sydney Zoo – Western Sydney's Wild Adventure
description: Come face to face with giraffes, gorillas, hippos and hundreds more animals at Sydney Zoo in Bungarribee Park — a brand new world-class zoo in Western Sydney.
longDescription:
Sydney Zoo opened in Bungarribee Park, Blacktown in 2019 — and in just a few years it has built a reputation as one of Australia's most impressive zoo experiences. Built from scratch on a purpose-designed site, every habitat is larger, more naturalistic and more animal-first than older facilities, which shows in the behaviour and wellbeing of the animals you see.

The headline acts are extraordinary. Giraffes pace through an open African savannah. Western lowland gorillas — one of the world's most endangered great apes — live in a vast forested enclosure. Hippos splash in a river habitat that lets you watch them underwater through floor-to-ceiling glass. Australian wildlife including koalas, wombats and wallabies round out a full day of discovery. With excellent parking, a good café and plenty of shaded seating, it is also one of the most practical family days out in Western Sydney.

Families can look forward to:
* Giraffes roaming an open African savannah — feeding opportunities available on selected days
* Western lowland gorillas in a spacious forested habitat — a genuinely rare encounter
* Watch hippos swimming underwater through panoramic glass viewing panels
* Koalas, wombats, wallabies and Australian reptiles in naturalistic bush settings
* Over 100 species across African, Asian and Australian wildlife zones
* Excellent café, picnic areas and plenty of shaded rest spots throughout the park
* Located next to Eastern Creek with ample free parking — 40 minutes from Sydney CBD
address: Bungarribee Park, Great Western Highway, Blacktown NSW 2148

title: ANZAC Memorial Hyde Park – Free Sunday Guided Tour
description: A free one-hour guided tour of the ANZAC Memorial in Hyde Park every Sunday at 10am — explore the stunning 1934 Art Deco architecture and hear the moving stories behind one of Sydney's most significant buildings.
longDescription:
If your family missed the ANZAC Day special tours on Saturday, the ANZAC Memorial offers its regular free guided tours every Sunday at 10am — and they are just as worthwhile any week of the year.

The memorial is a 1934 Art Deco masterpiece that honours the 226,000 men and women of NSW who served in the First World War. The hour-long highlights tour takes in the Hall of Memory and Hall of Service, explains the extraordinary symbolism built into the architecture, the sculptures by Rayner Hoff, and the thousands of names inscribed throughout the building. It is quietly magnificent — and children who've just watched the ANZAC Day march the day before will find the stories particularly resonant.

Families can look forward to:
* Free one-hour guided highlights tour every Sunday at 10am — no bookings needed
* Explore the stunning Art Deco architecture of one of Australia's finest memorials
* Discover the stories of NSW men and women commemorated within the building
* The Hall of Memory's domed ceiling and the Pool of Reflection are breathtaking
* Sculptures by renowned Australian artist Rayner Hoff throughout the building
* Open 9am–5pm daily with free entry — worth exploring independently too
* Located in Hyde Park South — combine with a picnic in the park afterwards
address: Hyde Park South, Liverpool Street, Sydney NSW 2000
costLabel: free entry and free guided tour

title: Art Gallery NSW – Free Family Sunday Visit
description: The Art Gallery of NSW is free to visit every day — on Sunday 26 April, combine free general admission with weekend family art-making activities, roving gallery educators and a picnic in the Domain.
longDescription:
The Art Gallery of New South Wales is one of Australia's finest cultural institutions — and one of its most generous, with free general admission always. Sunday 26 April is the perfect day to visit: the post-ANZAC-Day long weekend means the city is quieter than usual, and the gallery's weekend family programs are in full swing.

Across the two buildings — the classical heritage wing and the spectacular new Sydney Modern building — families can explore everything from Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander art to European masters, contemporary Australian works and striking photography. Weekend roving activities see gallery educators pop up with art-making materials inspired by works on display. The Domain parkland outside is perfect for a post-gallery picnic.

Families can look forward to:
* Free general admission to both the heritage building and Sydney Modern — always
* Weekend family art-making activities with roving gallery educators
* The stunning Sydney Modern building with spectacular harbour views from the roof terrace
* Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander galleries — one of the finest collections in Australia
* The Domain parkland right outside — perfect for a family picnic after the gallery
* Café and restaurant in both buildings for a relaxed family lunch
* Easy access via St James, Museum or Martin Place train stations

title: Biennale of Sydney – Free Family Art at White Bay Power Station
description: The 25th Biennale of Sydney transforms the spectacular White Bay Power Station into a free open art playground — with hands-on family workshops, immersive installations and interactive art for all ages.
longDescription:
Inside the cathedral-like halls of White Bay Power Station in Rozelle, one of Australia's most ambitious art events has thrown open its doors for free — and families are invited. The 25th Biennale of Sydney, themed 'Rememory', runs until June 2026 and fills this breathtaking heritage building with immersive installations, interactive artworks and hands-on creative experiences that are as engaging for a seven-year-old as they are for an adult.

White Bay Power Station is an industrial masterpiece in itself — towering turbine halls, soaring ceilings and raw industrial bones turned into a world-class arts venue. The Biennale has programmed regular Family Days with free drop-in art workshops led by artists, so kids don't just look at art, they make it. The Biennale also extends to other venues including the Art Gallery of NSW and the Chau Chak Wing Museum, making it easy to combine with a broader cultural day out.

Families can look forward to:
* Free general admission to one of Australia's biggest art events — no ticket required
* Spectacular White Bay Power Station — a heritage building unlike anything else in Sydney
* Family Days with free drop-in hands-on art workshops led by practising artists
* Immersive and interactive installations designed to engage visitors of all ages
* Multiple venues including Art Gallery NSW and Chau Chak Wing Museum
* Runs Tuesday to Sunday, 10am–5pm — great for a weekday or weekend visit
* Located in Rozelle (Inner West) — accessible via ferry to Balmain East or bus

title: Coogee Beach ANZAC Day Dawn Service
description: Join the Coogee community for a moving ANZAC Day dawn service on the beach — a beautiful, intimate local alternative to the city services, with the ocean as a backdrop.
longDescription:
While thousands gather at Martin Place for the main Sydney Dawn Service, the Coogee community gathers on its own beach at dawn on ANZAC Day for a service that is quieter, more intimate, and no less moving. With the Pacific Ocean stretching out behind the memorial and the early light catching the waves, it's a genuinely special way to mark the day — and a manageable experience for families with children.

Coogee Beach has long been a gathering place for the Eastern Suburbs community on ANZAC Day. The atmosphere is respectful and warm, with locals of all ages coming together to remember. For families, it's a wonderful opportunity to explain the significance of ANZAC Day in a setting that feels personal rather than overwhelming — and the beach is right there for a walk afterwards.

Families can look forward to:
* A free, community-run ANZAC Day dawn service right on the beach
* Beautiful ocean backdrop as the sun rises over the Pacific
* Intimate local atmosphere — quieter and more accessible than city services
* Easy to explain to children — a meaningful first ANZAC Day experience
* Coogee Beach right there for a family walk or breakfast after
* Close to Coogee Bay Road cafés for a post-service family breakfast
* Well-served by buses from Bondi Junction and the city

title: Waverley ANZAC Day Memorial Service – Waverley Park
description: Waverley Council's official ANZAC Day memorial service at Waverley Memorial Gardens — a local, family-friendly commemorative service with wreath-laying, followed by refreshments.
longDescription:
Every ANZAC Day, the Eastern Suburbs community gathers at Waverley Memorial Gardens in Waverley Park for a moving commemorative service that has been part of local life for generations. Starting at 7:45am, it's a civilised hour for families — no pre-dawn wake-up required — and the setting inside the memorial gardens is beautifully maintained and quiet.

The service includes a formal wreath-laying ceremony, a minute's silence, and traditional ANZAC Day readings. Light refreshments are provided at Waverley Park after the service, and guests are then invited to Bondi Junction RSL for further refreshments. For families looking to mark ANZAC Day in the Eastern Suburbs without the crowds of the CBD, this is the perfect local option.

title: Manly Harbour Village Sunday Markets

longDescription:
Every Sunday, Little Bayside Park in Manly comes alive with markets that have become a beloved institution on the Northern Beaches. Set right on the harbour with views across to the city, it's one of Sydney's most scenic market settings — and entry is completely free. Local artisans, fresh produce growers, food vendors and makers all set up stalls, and live music drifts through the park from mid-morning.

For families, the Manly Harbour Village markets are an easy, relaxed way to spend a Sunday morning. Kids can explore the stalls while parents browse, and the harbour foreshore is right there for a walk or a play. Combine it with a swim at Manly Beach (a short walk away) or breakfast at one of the many cafés along the Corso for a full day out on the Northern Beaches.

title: Australian Museum – Free Family Visit
description: Australia's oldest museum has free general admission — explore dinosaur skeletons, the Surviving Australia gallery, live animal presentations and a dedicated Kids Learning & Play Space.
longDescription:
Tucked behind Hyde Park in the CBD, the Australian Museum is one of the great free institutions of Sydney family life. General admission is free for everyone — and what you get inside is genuinely world-class: real dinosaur skeletons towering over you in the Dinosaur Gallery, the spectacular Wild Planet exhibition with more than 400 animals, hands-on spaces designed just for children, and the extraordinary First Nations collections that tell 65,000 years of Australian story.

The Kids Learning & Play Space is a purpose-built area for younger children — interactive, tactile and completely free to use during opening hours. Drop-in programs and live animal presentations run throughout the week, and the museum's café and courtyard are perfect for a mid-visit break. On April 26 (Sunday), the Frog and Tadpole Society is running a free special event in Hintze Hall — a rare chance to meet live rescued frogs and learn from experts.

Families can look forward to:
* Free general admission — no tickets, no booking required for general entry
* Real dinosaur skeletons in the Dinosaur Gallery — always a crowd favourite
* Wild Planet exhibition with 400+ animals from around the world
* Kids Learning & Play Space — interactive and designed for young visitors
* First Nations galleries — one of the finest collections in Australia
* Live animal presentations and drop-in programs throughout the week
* Special: Frog and Tadpole Society event in Hintze Hall on Sunday 26 April (10am–2pm)
* Right behind Hyde Park — easy to combine with a picnic or visit to the ANZAC Memorial

title: MCA Sydney – Free Entry for Kids & Families
description: The Museum of Contemporary Art at Circular Quay is always free for anyone under 18 — with rooftop harbour views, family art trails and drop-in studio activities throughout the year.
longDescription:
Right on the edge of Sydney Harbour at Circular Quay, the Museum of Contemporary Art is one of those places that Sydneysiders sometimes take for granted but visitors travel across the world to see. And the best news for families: entry is always free for anyone under 18, Australian residents and members. There is no catch and no booking required for general admission.

The MCA's collection spans painting, sculpture, photography, video, performance and digital art from Australian and international artists. The building itself is spectacular — a heritage art deco exterior with a modern rooftop terrace offering some of the best harbour views in Sydney, including direct sightlines to the Opera House and Harbour Bridge. Family art trails help kids engage with the works, and drop-in studio workshops run regularly throughout the year.

Families can look forward to:
* Free entry for all children under 18 — always, no booking required
* World-class contemporary art collection in a stunning Circular Quay location
* Rooftop terrace with iconic Sydney Harbour and Opera House views
* Family art trails designed to help kids connect with the artworks
* Drop-in studio art-making activities for younger visitors
* Café and rooftop restaurant with harbour views for a family lunch
* Walk to Circular Quay ferry wharves, the Opera House and Rocks foreshore
* Open Wed–Mon, 10am–5pm (closed Tuesdays)

title: Blaxland Riverside Park – Free Water Play & Nature Playground
description: NSW's largest outdoor water play facility at Sydney Olympic Park — completely free. Water jets, splash pads, climbing structures and riverside walking paths across 5 hectares of parkland.
longDescription:
If you haven't been to Blaxland Riverside Park at Sydney Olympic Park, you're missing one of Western Sydney's great free family secrets. Spread across five hectares on the banks of the Parramatta River, this park is home to NSW's largest outdoor water play facility — and it's completely free to use. No tickets, no booking, just show up with bathers, a towel and a packed lunch.

The water play area features jets, sprays, splash channels and play structures that keep children occupied for hours. Beyond the water play, the park has extensive nature-based play areas, cycling and walking paths along the riverside, picnic shelters and barbecue facilities. It's the kind of place where families arrive for an hour and end up staying all day — and given it sits within the broader Sydney Olympic Park precinct, there's plenty more to explore nearby.

Families can look forward to:
* NSW's largest free outdoor water play facility — splash pads, jets and channels
* Five hectares of riverside parkland with nature-based play and picnic areas
* Free entry, free parking, free barbecue facilities — just bring food and bathers
* Walking and cycling paths along the Parramatta River
* Part of Sydney Olympic Park — combine with Bicentennial Park or the Aquatic Centre
* Great for all ages from toddlers to tweens
* Train to Lidcombe then bus, or drive with easy parking

description: Explore a moving free exhibition at the RPA Museum by Sydney artist Roma Lestal — a collection of small, meaningful objects shared by hospital patients about the things that brought them comfort and healing. Includes a free Amazing History Treasure Hunt activity booklet perfect for curious kids. A gentle, thoughtful outing that sparks big conversations about care, kindness and what matters most.
venue: RPA Museum Art Heritage Gallery, Royal Prince Alfred Hospital, Camperdown

title: Broken Glass & Blue Bottles – Free Surf Photography at Bondi Pavilion
description: Step inside a free photographic exhibition capturing the raw spirit of Sydney surf culture — from Bondi to Bronte. Photographer Luke Kennedy of Tracks Magazine documents the characters, waves and moments that define Australian surfing. Displayed in the stunning art gallery inside the iconic Bondi Pavilion, it's a brilliant free outing for surf-loving families and school-age kids.
venue: Bondi Pavilion Art Gallery, Queen Elizabeth Drive, Bondi Beach

title: Spark in the Park – Free Outdoor Stories & Songs for Under 5s
description: Head to Broadarrow Reserve in Maroubra for this free drop-in outdoor storytime run by Randwick City Library. Look for the colourful Spark truck — there'll be stories, songs and play for little ones aged 0–5 years. No bookings needed, just turn up and enjoy a fun morning in the park. Part of Randwick's 2026 Year of Kindness program. Weather permitting.

title: Plant with Us – Free Mother's Day Tree Planting at Heffron Park
description: Celebrate Mother's Day by getting your hands in the earth together! Randwick City Council hosts this free family tree-planting morning at Heffron Park, Maroubra — helping create wildlife habitat for future generations. Two sessions available. Wear sturdy shoes and bring gloves, a hat and a water bottle. Bookings via Humanitix are required.

title: The Saturday Circle – Free Family Morning at Randwick Sustainability Hub
description: A free monthly community gathering at Randwick's Sustainability Hub with something for everyone — outdoor storytime for little ones, Lego building, toy swaps, community birding, learning to grow food and more. A hands-on, nature-connected morning for families of all ages on the second Saturday of each month.
venue: Randwick Sustainability Hub, 27 Munda Street, Randwick
